rationale: C17 is the closest in form: both are short numbered executive orders amending an earlier military regulation through textual changes and concluding with an effective-date provision. C23 and C13 likewise amend prior regulations by numbered insertions or replacements. These similarities, however, are standard amendment machinery rather than distinctive or materially shared drafting. None of the candidates contains the child's substantive aerial-flight requirements, its escalating one-, two-, and three-month flight formulas, or comparable administrative machinery. Shared military terminology or coverage of reserve components does not establish a reusable template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The words "reserve components of the armed services" are substituted for the words "National Guard" occurring in the title and preamble of the said order.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: C17: The words "Air Force," are inserted after the word "Army," wherever such word occurs in the said order and in the title thereof.
shared_material.explanation: Both make a targeted terminology change in an earlier order, including its title, but this is routine amendatory drafting.

shared_material.child_excerpt: This order shall become effective on June 1, 1949, except that ... it shall become effective on July 1, 1949.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: C23: This order shall be effective as of December 1, 1948.
shared_material.explanation: Both end with an effective-date clause, which is boilerplate and does not demonstrate material templating.
